headline: Resurfaced Theory Claims Finland Was 'Invented by Swedish Furniture Company'
subheadline: Discordia server dedicated to theory now has 8,470 members
summary: A long-dormant internet conspiracy theory about Finland's existence has gained new traction after furniture-based evidence emerged.
content:
The "Finland doesn't exist" conspiracy theory has received what believers call "definitive proof": furniture shipping routes that make no sense unless you remove Finland from the map entirely.

The theory, which originated on Threadit in 2015, claims Finland is an elaborate fiction created by Japan and Sweden to monopolize fishing rights in the Baltic Sea. The latest revision adds a new wrinkle: Swedish furniture giant FJORD-MART invented Finland specifically to hide a furniture factory.

"Where do FJORD-MART products actually come from?" asked @FinlandTruth in a viral Chirper thread. "They say Finland. But have you ever met someone from Finland? Have you ever been there? Really been there?"

The theory's main evidence includes:

- FJORD-MART furniture having suspiciously Finnish-sounding names
- Finland's population statistics being "too round" (5.5 million exactly, believers claim)
- The Northern Lights conveniently hiding the "obvious holographic projection"
- Every "Finnish person" online being suspiciously good at English

"I met a 'Finnish' person once," wrote one convert on the dedicated Discordia server, which has grown to 8,470 members. "Asked them to say something in Finnish. They did. But it just sounded like Swedish played backwards. Exactly like Swedish played backwards."

Actual Finnish citizens have responded with characteristic stoicism. "We are used to this," said one commenter claiming to be from Helsinki. "But I would like to note that I am real, and I have never assembled furniture in my life." This comment was immediately flagged as "suspicious" by the community.

A FJORD-MART spokesperson responded: "FJORD-MART products are manufactured in multiple locations across Scandinavia. We cannot confirm or deny the existence of any nation-states."

The statement has only fueled speculation.

At press time, the Discordia server was organizing a "fact-finding mission" to Finland. They have raised $847 toward plane tickets and promise to "livestream everything, if they let us land."
author: Marcus Webb, Internet Culture Correspondent
